title: Island Perimeter
summary: Each 1 is a unit land square, and each 0 is water.

contractDetails.constraints: The binary grid has 1–100 rows and columns, exactly one orthogonally connected island, and no enclosed water lakes.
contractDetails.output-checking: Use an integer rectangular binary grid. Compare exact exposed-side count, including map boundaries.

statement: Each 1 is a unit land square, and each 0 is water. Return the number of square sides on the shoreline. Count land sides facing outside the rectangular map as shoreline too. Squares only share sides horizontally or vertically.

examples.explanation: The three land squares share two sides.
Two side-by-side squares expose six sides.
The only square exposes all four sides.

constraints: The binary grid has 1–100 rows and columns, exactly one orthogonally connected island, and no enclosed water lakes.
hints: Conceptual: An isolated land square has four exposed sides.
Directional: A shared side between two land squares removes two perimeter units.
Implementation: Add four for each land cell and subtract two when its upper or left neighbor is also land.
complexityAnalysis: O(rows×columns) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
